item.title: House Democrats move to probe Trump family, top administration officials
item.description: House Democrats plan investigations into Trump family's finances, DHS conduct and the administration's handling of Jeffrey Epstein files.
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: The top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee is laying the groundwork for long-promised investigations into the Trump administration, which are set to begin with the new Congress in January. Representative Robert Garcia of California, who is expected to lead the House Oversight Committee when Democrats take control, sent letters directing members of President Donald Trump’s family and top administration officials to preserve documents. The move is an early step towards launching investigations into the president and his administration. The letters, released on Wednesday, cover a wide range of potential investigations, including alleged financial conflicts involving Trump’s family, misconduct at the Department of Homeland Security and the administration’s handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein. “Oversight Democrats are fighting to put an end to this Administration’s self-dealing, misconduct, and abuse,” Garcia said in a statement. “These investigations will lay the groundwork for legislation which helps all Americans. This is just the beginning.” Those targeted by the letters include two of Trump’s sons, Vice President JD Vance, White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law. The letters offer an early glimpse of how Democrats plan to use their newly won congressional majority to scrutinise Trump and his administration. As favourable election results rolled in for Democrats on the night of the midterms, Garcia posted a warning on social media: “Lawyer up.”

item.title: Anthropic raises $81 bn, set to secure $1.8 trn valuation in Nasdaq debut
item.description: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, valuing the Claude maker at $1.5 trillion. Strong opening indications pointed to a potential $1.8 trillion valuation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic was on course to secure a $1.8 trillion valuation when its shares start trading on Thursday, in a historic debut that pits promises of artificial intelligence (AI) as an economic game-changer against fears of a market bubble and risks to humanity. The stock was set to open at $99.82, about 20 per cent higher than the initial public offering (IPO) price of $83, according to indications as of 8:20 pm IST on Thursday. The Claude chatbot maker’s upsized IPO, together with Tuesday’s earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia, signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week. The strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to a sector where euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks. AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-centre-sceptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections. Investors who once embraced the boom have turned sceptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the mounting debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns. Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market debut on record after increasing the size of its offering, in a deal that values the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion and defied concerns over AI and tech fundraising. In a sign of strong investor demand, Anthropic priced its shares at $83 each, above its initial range of $70 to $78. Reuters was first to report on Wednesday that Anthropic, the first major frontier AI model developer to float, had increased the number of shares it was selling by about 19 per cent to 980 million. Anthropic’s IPO eclipses the debut of Elon Musk’s SpaceX in June. Its total deal size is $107.3 billion, including another $26 billion that Anthropic is raising through a private placement of shares, the filings showed. Nasdaq futures rose nearly 2 per cent on Thursday, bolstering expectations for a strong Anthropic debut and reviving sentiment around AI stocks. Chipmakers and cloud companies, which have raised hundreds of billions of dollars to fund their massive spending plans, have in recent weeks come under pressure due to valuation concerns, mounting AI infrastructure costs and the sudden exit of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang. Anthropic has, meanwhile, faced questions about its outlook and ability to sustain rapid growth as competition intensifies. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are lead underwriters for Anthropic’s IPO, which has a 22-bank underwriting syndicate. Anthropic’s annualised revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to its IPO filing. Underscoring its growing business foothold, Anthropic said it had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year. But to sustain that growth, Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026. Anthropic also incurred an additional $5 billion in computing costs in the third quarter, reducing the revenue generated per dollar of computing capacity. Revenue rose to $16.96 billion in the third quarter, up 47 per cent from the second. The company reported an operating loss of $567 million, compared with operating income of $974 million in the previous quarter. The net loss narrowed to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating items related to bonds convertible into its shares. Anthropic has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners, including Amazon and Alphabet’s Google, to train and operate AI models.

item.title: Walmart lifts annual forecasts, flags $2 bn fuel and transport cost burden
item.description: Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 sales and earnings forecasts, but warned that higher diesel and transportation costs have added about $2 billion to expenses this year.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Walmart lifts annual forecasts, flags $2 bn fuel and transport cost burden

Walmart lifts annual forecasts, flags $2 bn fuel and transport cost burden Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 sales and earnings forecasts, but warned that higher diesel and transportation costs have added about $2 billion to expenses this year.

Walmart has raised its annual forecasts on strong e-commerce and membership growth, while warning that higher fuel and transportation expenses are adding pressure to costs ahead of the holiday shopping season. (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 19 2026 | 11:20 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Rising fuel costs are complicating Walmart's efforts to keep prices low even as strong growth in its delivery and membership businesses prompted the retailer to raise annual forecasts ahead of the crucial holiday shopping season. The world's largest retailer, seen as a bellwether for US consumer health, reported a 5.2% rise in third-quarter revenue to $188.84 billion, beating expectations. It now expects fiscal 2027 net sales to grow 4.9% to 5.2%, up from its previous forecast of 4% to 5%, but still below analysts' expectations for growth of 5.5%, according to data compiled by LSEG. CEO John Furner said surging diesel and transportation costs had added about $2 billion in incremental expenses this year and could hamper efforts to keep prices low as consumers head into the holiday shopping season.

"We will do everything we can in terms of efficiency," Furner said on a post-earnings call, adding that pricing "really depends on transportation costs and input costs as we move forward." Also Read

HOLIDAY PLANS Walmart has cut prices on thousands of grocery and general merchandise items this year as Americans seek cheaper options amid high inflation and an Iran War that has pushed up fuel prices. Consumer sentiment, while improving in November, remains weak. Rising freight and logistics costs have squeezed profits across the retail and consumer goods industries, though Walmart has partly offset the impact through nearly $3 billion in tariff refunds, Furner said.

Still, executives struck an upbeat tone about the holiday shopping season. "It's game time," Furner said, noting that Walmart had sold 1 million more Thanksgiving turkeys than a year earlier after cutting the price of its holiday meal basket to its lowest since the programme was launched in 2022. The retailer has leaned on its stores as "digital fulfilment nodes" for e-commerce orders and its higher-margin third-party marketplace, which posted gains during the quarter. That has helped support sales as growth in store visits has slowed from a year earlier. "The margin story is outrunning the traffic story right now," said David Wagner, head of equity at Aptus Capital Advisors.

The retailer has pushed deeper into membership, e-commerce and marketplace businesses to diversify revenue and support margins. Last month, it launched a bundled membership offer for its Walmart+ loyalty programme and its Sam's Club wholesale unit. Membership fee revenue rose by double digits in the three months through October. Its push into faster delivery has also helped drive repeat purchases, while customers using the service were more likely to sign up for its membership programme, the company said. Overall, US e-commerce sales increased 23%, compared with 28% growth a year earlier. Walmart raised its annual adjusted earnings forecast to $2.84 to $2.89 per share from $2.80 to $2.87 previously. Analysts expect $2.88 per share.

Adjusted earnings of 65 cents per share edged past estimates, while operating expenses rose 5% to $40.01 billion. Walmart shares fell about 2%. The stock has gained about 14% this year and is on track for a fourth straight annual gain.

item.title: GTA VI wins rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City after 13-year wait
item.description: After 13 years in the making, GTA VI has launched worldwide to strong early reviews, with Sensor Tower estimating sales of over 17 million copies worth more than $1.65 billion.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / GTA VI wins rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City after 13-year wait

GTA VI wins rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City after 13-year wait After 13 years in the making, GTA VI has launched worldwide to strong early reviews, with Sensor Tower estimating sales of over 17 million copies worth more than $1.65 billion.

Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI has launched worldwide after a 13-year wait, drawing strong early reviews and significant player interest as the latest instalment in one of the world's best-selling video game franchises. (Screenshot)

Reuters 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 19 2026 | 11:12 PM IST

Listen to This Article

After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolled out across the globe on Thursday, gaining rapturous early reviews for the most anticipated video game release in history. The game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, raced to the top of Metacritic's all-time gaming leaderboard with a score of 99, a mark matched by only one other title, Nintendo's 1998 classic "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time". The rollout began as the clock struck midnight in New Zealand and moved across time zones from Tokyo to Miami, prompting launch parties, posts from world leaders and even some companies giving staff the day off to play.

"It is the best game that's ever been made and we're only 20 minutes deep," said 33-year-old Asif Mir as he started to play and livestream just after midnight in Sydney. In London, gamers counted down to the release at parties across the city. Also Read

Gamers skip work, crowd gaming cafes for GTA VI as PM Modi joins the buzz

Grand Theft Auto 6: New Vice City, record viewership, and global frenzy

Get GTA 6 in minutes: Blinkit rolls out quick delivery in 11 cities

Grand Theft Auto VI wins rave reviews as gamers return to Vice City

GTA 6 India launch: First impressions, prices, editions and download size

"Today has been a day that I have waited for my whole life," said 20-year-old influencer Archie Whitby. "To be living it, it feels almost dystopian. It doesn't feel real." Miami, the inspiration for the game's fictional Vice City setting, was one of the last places to get in on the action. The city's NBA team, the Miami Heat, celebrated with a Vice City-themed match against the Milwaukee Bucks, with the court and stadium adorned with the game's colours of neon pink and blue.

Mia Pazan travelled to Miami for the launch. "I came here, number one, because I love GTA VI. I played literally all the games," she said, adding that as a Latina woman she loved the fact that there was a protagonist — co-lead character Lucia Caminos — reflecting her identity. "I really identify with Lucia a lot," she added. Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles, with many taking time off work — or calling in sick — to play the latest instalment in a franchise that since its 1997 debut has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

"It's the Star Wars of this generation," said Joost van Dreunen, adjunct professor at NYU Stern School of Business. "It's a synchronized, shared event. So millions of people will all want to be there the first couple of days, the first few weeks of experiencing it as it goes live." Strong initial reviews of the game — available on Sony's PlayStation 5 and Microsoft's Xbox Series X and S consoles — helped push Take-Two Interactive's US shares higher on Wednesday. GREAT STRESS RELIEF' FOR FEMALE GAMERS The original "Grand Theft Auto" looks basic by today's standards, with a storyline — stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates — that angered politicians and parents, even as it delighted fans.

But as the series progressed it became increasingly sophisticated, mixing its trademark crime, driving and morally dubious missions with activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirising US culture. "Grand Theft Auto V", released in 2013, was set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles. The action now moves to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, in the state of Leonida, the game's take on Florida. Play will switch between two leading characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. They are partners in crime and romantically involved — just how romantically will be up to the player. There will be nightclubs, gun stores, scuba diving and a zoo. But much remains to be revealed.

GTA VI could prove less provocative than its predecessors, said Tore Olsson, a professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville. "There's no doubt that Jason and Lucia of VI will be criminals, and they'll be regularly breaking the law," said Olsson. "But I don't think the new game will require players to enact wanton slaughter, and it may indeed penalize those who choose to play that way." Having Lucia as a lead character should help address complaints about a lack of playable female characters in previous iterations of GTA. Women will be an estimated four out of 10 GTA VI players in the US, according to a Bain survey.

"Since you can do all that brutal stuff like running people over or hitting them, my first thought was that it's mostly for male players," said 30-year-old Tokyo worker Suzana Onoda. "After trying it out, well, I think getting to beat people up is a great stress relief for women as well." STRONG REVIEWS: 'TRULY ASTONISHING', 'A MASTERPIECE' Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated that more than 17 million copies had been sold so far for over $1.65 billion. With the main part of the game estimated to take around 50 hours to complete, full reactions were not available immediately. But initial reviews from gaming industry experts were almost universal in their high praise.

Entertainment website GamesRadar+ said Rockstar had built a world of "truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality". The release "will be talked about for years to come" and was "well worth the 13-year wait", said PC Games. Various outlets called it a "masterpiece". While some economists have warned about lost productivity as gamers take time off from work, consumer analysts said the economy could also receive a boost from sales of the game, consoles, storage upgrades and even food delivery services. In India, home to hundreds of millions of gamers, Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted Grand Theft Auto-inspired social media content and some firms gave employees the day off.

On Australia's southern island of Tasmania, family-run fragrance shop Whiff-it! will close for a week after 20-year-old Jonah Bowen-Brown persuaded his mother to give him and his brother time off to play. "She was really against it at first," said Bowen-Brown. "I had to say, mum, please, please, I need it... I've been waiting 13 years to play the game."
